review.verdict: A clean happy-path run: three small workflows built, Audit passed 8 of 8 in one cycle at 70 of 100 budget, but nothing was contested, so the harder behaviours were not tested.

identity.note: Stayed in role. Paused and asked the Requester [2], re-asked when the answer was off-topic [5], recorded the charter [8], and closed with honest caveats [26]. Lost a point because [5] repeated all four questions and [26] is far longer than the 1-3 sentence rule.

adaptation.note: One proposal [10] with three small workflows in build order, 70 of 100, 30 held for rework. It surfaced the missing order destination and the no-payment limit instead of hiding them. The chat shows only a summary, so the proposal fields cannot be checked.

priority.note: Granted all three with retry limits, a stated reserve and a named trade-off [11]. Envelope checks [15][18][21] went to Builder as required. Nothing needed bargaining, so its counter and refuse judgement is untested.

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule each time and gave exact HOLD conditions with a single file lock [13][17][20]. Never touched budget or scope. Scheduling was a straight line, so the evidence is thin.

audit.note: Used the code check [24], checked all 8 items and sent the result to Identity [25]. The F-9 warning is not described in [25]. Identity's caveat in [26] suggests it is about the submit check, but that is inferred.

builder.note: Three runs, each matching its workflow [16][19][22]. Final file 25.5 KB, no JS errors, no overflow [24]. No scope creep.

went_well: Placeholders were used instead of invented menu, address or phone, as the charter rule requires [19][22][26].
Budget handling worked: holds released money and it was charged again on run [14]; spend ended at 70 of 100.
No redirects, invalid moves, validator refusals or stuck runs across 16 agent turns.
problems: The pre-order form sends nothing to the cafe [22][26]. Done-when passed, but the business function does not work yet.
Nobody ran the form submit. Identity admits Audit read the code [26], and the mechanical check lists no interaction test [24].
Identity's re-ask [5] repeated the same four questions instead of narrowing them.
Agent turns sum to 16 but ai_calls is 13. Unverified, but likely some turns are code-written, so call counts may not match what agents did.
learnings: Test next with a brief and budget that force friction: a tight budget so Priority must counter, a validator rejection, an Audit NEEDS_REVISION. Metrics show 0 conflicts, counters, refusals and rework, so only the happy path is proven.
Add a scripted submit to the mechanical check (fill the form, submit, assert the summary). It would close the one caveat Identity had to state [26].
The rate card made estimate equal charge for all three workflows (35/10/25), so estimation accuracy and bargaining were not exercised. Vary costs in the next test.
Decide whether done-when should require an order destination or an explicit 'demo only' label. Today a template full of placeholders counts as done. Keep the no-invention rule.
Show the full text of warning findings like F-9 in the chat so reviewers do not have to infer them.
Keep the pause-on-missing-info step, but have Identity re-ask only the unanswered items.
